# phase-097 — Parse and format dates from text, the way time.format cannot today

## You must change `src/`

This phase declares `must_touch: [src/]`. The gate fails the phase unless at
least one changed file falls under it. Writing tests, documentation or a report
is not enough — if you finish without touching that area, the phase fails on
exactly that check.


## Evidence — verified finding

```
phase-096 gives Redblue a date value but no way to get one from text or print one in a chosen shape. time.format takes a Unix timestamp and a format string, and time.unix parses one fixed 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' layout, so a program cannot read an ISO-8601 timestamp with a zone, cannot read the format another system emits, and cannot control the output shape. Every real program that reads data from somewhere else - a log line, a CSV column, an HTTP header - needs this, and the current single hardcoded layout is the reason it cannot.
```

**Re-verify this before you change anything.** If the finding no longer
reproduces on `main`, stop and write that to `FINDINGS.md` — a stale phase must
never be "fixed" by inventing a change.

## Goal

Give the date value parsing and formatting: parse ISO-8601 including an offset and fractional seconds, format to a caller-chosen layout, and convert between the date value and a Unix timestamp. Extend the existing time.unix and time.format to route through the date value rather than remaining a separate implementation, so there is one date model in the runtime rather than two that can disagree. A malformed timestamp must raise a catchable error naming the offending characters, never a panic and never a silently wrong value.

6. Write `REPORT.md` in the exact shape required by `AGENTS.md` section 4.

## Definition of done

- [ ] an ISO-8601 timestamp with a zone offset parses to a date value equal to the same instant expressed in UTC - asserted on literal values, not on round-tripping through the same code
- [ ] formatting a date to a chosen layout produces the exact expected text, including padding and a zero-padded month against a single-digit month
- [ ] the existing time.unix and time.format still return what they returned for the inputs they already handled, with the existing tests passing unmodified
- [ ] a malformed timestamp raises a catchable Error::Runtime naming the position that failed to parse, and no input makes the parser panic
- [ ] a timestamp with fractional seconds preserves the fraction, and one without a zone is interpreted under the stance phase-096 documented
- [ ] the tree-walker and the bytecode VM parse and format identically, compared as data across both engines
- [ ] SPEC.md documents the accepted layouts, including what is NOT accepted, so the limits are explicit
- [ ] edge_* tests cover Feb 29 in a leap year, a leap second refused rather than accepted silently, an empty string, a date-only string, a timezone-less string, and a string with trailing garbage
